chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Al-Husayn ibn Nasr, from his father, from 'Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wanted to ride to visit one of his Shias, so he said: 'O Jabir, accompany me.' So I followed him. When he reached the door of the house, a young son of his came out to us. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: 'What is your name?' He said, 'Muhammad.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'By what are you teknonymed (kunya)?' He said, 'With Ali.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: 'You have guarded yourself against Satan with intense guarding. Indeed, when Satan hears a caller calling out, 'O Muhammad! O Ali!', he melts just as lead melts, until when he hears a caller calling out with the name of an enemy from our enemies, he trembles and struts.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the names Muhammad and Ali in relation to Satan according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir illustrates the cosmological impact of the names Muhammad and Ali, describing how Satan melts like lead when hearing them, contrasting with his agitation at the names of their enemies. This highlights the Shia theological concept of the spiritual authority (*wilayah*) of the Ahl al-Bayt, where their names serve as a source of comfort for the faithful and a source of distress for their adversaries. The incident underscores the practical significance of naming children after the Imams as a means of invoking divine protection and spiritual affinity.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, from Al Husayn Bin Nasr, from his father, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> wanted to ride over to one of his<sup>asws</sup> Shias to bid him farewell, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Jabir! Accompany me’. So I followed him<sup>asws</sup>. So when he<sup>asws</sup> ended up to the door of the house, there came out to us a young boy. So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘What is your name?’ He said, ‘Muhammad’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘In what have you been teknonymed?’ So he said, ‘With Ali’. So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘You have agonised the Satan<sup>la</sup> with an intense agony. When the Satan<sup>la</sup> hears a caller calling out, ‘O Muhammad! O Ali!’, he<sup>la</sup> melts just like the melting of the lead, until when he<sup>la</sup> hears a caller calling out with a name of an enemy from our<sup>asws</sup> enemies, he<sup>la</sup> swings and struts’.
en.sarwar: 12. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Muslim from al-Husayn ibn Nasr from his father from ‘Amr ibn Shamir from Jabir who has said the following:

“Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once wanted to visit one of his followers because he was ill. He (the Imam) told me to follow him and I followed him (the Imam). When he (the Imam) arrived at his door his small son came out and abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asked, ‘What is your name?’ He replied, ‘It is Muhammad.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘What is your Kunyah ?’ He replied, ‘It is Ali.’ Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘You have fortified yourself against Satan very intensely. When Satan hears someone calling O Muhammad, O Ali, Satan melts like lead until he hears someone calling with the names of our enemies; he becomes excited and swaggers.’”
